name: Dentists
intro: Make patient education clearer and practice workflows easier, with the dentist in control.
caution: Educational workflows only. Do not upload identifiable patient records or images to consumer AI. Clinical tools require practice approval, appropriate data agreements, local regulatory checks and dentist review.

tools.name: Overjet
tools.fit: Explore dental AI for image-supported clinical review and practice workflows. Request a demonstration of your specific intended use.
tools.access: Practice demo / contract; confirm scope and integration

tools.name: ADA AI resources
tools.fit: Understand dental AI terminology, limitations and practice considerations before selecting a product.
tools.access: Professional reference; not an AI generator

tools.name: Microsoft Copilot
tools.fit: Explore general-purpose drafting for public or synthetic, non-sensitive material. This is not a clinical or estimating system.
tools.access: Use an organization-approved account and check current data terms and limits

useCases.title: Turn approved instructions into a patient-friendly explainer
useCases.summary: Prepare a readable take-home handout without inventing clinical advice.
useCases.inputs: Your practice-approved instruction sheet; reading level; language; no patient identifiers.
steps: Select a generic instruction sheet already approved by the dentist.
In a practice-approved writing assistant, request a plain-language version using only that source.
Compare every instruction with the source; have the dentist approve translations and final wording.
useCases.prompt: Using only the approved text below, draft a one-page plain-language handout. Preserve all warnings and contact instructions. Do not add medicines, doses or advice. Mark unclear wording for clinician review. [approved text]
useCases.output: A draft handout plus a list of passages needing review.
useCases.review: Confirm every clinical statement, translation and contact number. Provide the original instructions when needed.

useCases.title: Evaluate a dental imaging AI pilot
useCases.summary: Run a controlled evaluation of a specialist tool before changing practice workflows.
useCases.inputs: Approved evaluation images; intended-use documentation; clinician review rubric.
steps: Ask the vendor for device status, supported image types, privacy terms and integration requirements.
Use an approved evaluation environment; compare AI annotations with independent dentist assessments.
Record misses, false positives and workflow issues; decide whether a supervised pilot is justified.
useCases.prompt: Vendor evaluation checklist: intended use, jurisdiction, compatible imaging, data retention, disagreement handling, audit trail and training. Answer from supplied documentation only.
useCases.output: A pilot scorecard and documented go / no-go decision.
useCases.review: Annotations support review; the dentist determines findings and treatment. No accuracy claim is made here.

useCases.title: Draft a practice FAQ
useCases.summary: Answer routine questions about hours, booking and office policies.
useCases.inputs: Public practice policies and contact information.
steps: Collect current policies in one approved source.
Draft short answers and a clear escalation instruction for clinical questions.
Test ambiguous questions; publish only staff-reviewed answers.
useCases.prompt: Draft 10 FAQs using these office policies only. If information is missing, say to contact the office. Do not answer diagnosis or treatment questions. [policies]
useCases.output: A reviewed FAQ for the website or reception team.
useCases.review: Check hours, fees and policies. Never promise insurance coverage or treatment outcomes.

name: Doctors
intro: Explore documentation and communication workflows that keep clinical decisions with the care team.
caution: These are workflow examples, not medical advice. Use organization-approved systems, required patient consent and appropriate privacy agreements. A clinician must review clinical output before it enters the record or reaches a patient.

tools.name: Microsoft Dragon Copilot
tools.fit: Explore AI-assisted clinical documentation and clinician workflows.
tools.access: Organization procurement; confirm region, EHR and role support

tools.name: Dragon Copilot documentation
tools.fit: Read product capabilities and deployment guidance before a supervised pilot.

useCases.title: Create a reviewed visit-note draft
useCases.summary: Use an approved documentation assistant to draft, then reconcile, an encounter note.
useCases.inputs: Approved recording workflow, required consent and clinician documentation template.
steps: Confirm the organization has approved the tool, consent process and EHR workflow.
Capture an encounter through the approved system and generate a draft in the required format.
Reconcile the draft against the encounter; correct errors and sign only after clinician review.
useCases.prompt: For a synthetic training transcript only: organize the provided facts into the specified note headings. Do not infer diagnoses, normal findings, medication doses or missing history. Mark gaps.
useCases.output: A clinician-reviewed note with omissions and corrections resolved.
useCases.review: Check negations, speakers, allergies, medicines, doses and follow-up. Never auto-sign.

useCases.title: Draft an understandable visit summary
useCases.summary: Translate approved clinician instructions into accessible language.
useCases.inputs: Final clinician-approved instructions with identifiers removed for any general-purpose demonstration.
steps: Start from the approved plan rather than a model-generated treatment recommendation.
Request a plain-language draft that preserves every instruction and escalation detail.
Have the clinician check completeness and an appropriate reviewer check translated versions.
useCases.prompt: Rewrite only the supplied approved instructions in plain language. Preserve all numbers and warnings exactly. Add no medical advice. List anything ambiguous. [synthetic instructions]
useCases.output: A patient-summary draft and a review checklist.
useCases.review: Do not send until the clinician approves. Confirm that accessibility changes preserve meaning.

useCases.title: Prepare a referral-letter draft
useCases.summary: Organize verified information into a referral for clinician approval.
useCases.inputs: Verified reason for referral, relevant history and approved organizational template.
steps: Use an approved clinical environment and the minimum necessary information.
Draft the letter from supplied facts, explicitly marking missing fields.
Review recipients, urgency and attachments before securely sending.
useCases.prompt: Using this synthetic case and template, draft a referral. Do not invent examination findings, urgency or test results. Put [needs clinician input] where information is missing.
useCases.output: A reviewed referral letter with verified attachments.
useCases.review: The clinician decides urgency and destination; staff verify secure delivery.

name: Teachers
intro: Build lesson materials and feedback that fit your classroom, curriculum and learners.
caution: Use school-approved tools. Keep student identifiers and sensitive records out of general prompts. Teachers verify content and make grading and learning-support decisions.

tools.name: MagicSchool
tools.fit: Explore educator tools for planning, rubrics and classroom communication.
tools.access: Teacher access and district offerings; check current limits

tools.name: MagicSchool educator platform
tools.fit: Explore deployment, training and school policy resources.
tools.access: Confirm school approval and student-access terms

useCases.title: Build a lesson with a useful exit ticket
useCases.summary: Turn a curriculum objective into a teachable sequence and quick understanding check.
useCases.inputs: Grade level; exact standard; lesson duration; available materials.
steps: Paste the standard and identify prerequisite knowledge without student names.
Generate a sequence with modeling, guided practice, independent work and an exit ticket.
Solve all examples yourself and adapt pacing to your actual class.
useCases.prompt: Plan a 40-minute grade 4 lesson on rounding whole numbers to the nearest thousand. Include a number-line example, two misconceptions, five practice questions and a three-question exit ticket with a separate answer key.
useCases.output: An editable lesson outline, worksheet and checked answer key.
useCases.review: Verify alignment, arithmetic, reading load and accessibility.

useCases.title: Create reading supports from one text
useCases.summary: Prepare scaffolds without changing the learning objective.
useCases.inputs: A passage you have permission to use; vocabulary goals; curriculum objective.
steps: Select a short authorized passage and define the common learning goal.
Request vocabulary support, chunked instructions and an extension activity.
Compare versions with the original and check that key facts and challenge remain appropriate.
useCases.prompt: Using this permitted passage, create a vocabulary glossary, chunked reading questions and an extension task. Keep all original facts. Do not label students by ability. [passage]
useCases.output: Three support options tied to one objective.
useCases.review: Check fidelity, cultural assumptions and learning needs. Do not upload IEPs or student records.

useCases.title: Create a rubric and formative feedback bank
useCases.summary: Make expectations clear while keeping assessment with the teacher.
useCases.inputs: Assignment prompt; learning goals; anonymized or synthetic sample.
steps: Define success criteria before requesting a draft rubric.
Generate observable descriptors and feedback examples for each criterion.
Calibrate against sample work and revise before using with students.
useCases.prompt: Draft a four-level rubric for a grade 4 evidence-based paragraph. Use observable criteria for claim, evidence and explanation. Add encouraging feedback examples. Do not assign a student grade.
useCases.output: A calibrated rubric and reusable feedback suggestions.
useCases.review: The teacher assesses work and checks bias; do not use automated output as the final grade.

name: Painters & artists
intro: Explore visual concepts for artists and practical planning for painting contractors.
caution: AI previews are concepts. Screens and generated images do not reproduce physical paint exactly. Measure on site and confirm finishes with real samples.

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.fit: Generate and edit visual concepts for authorized creative projects.
tools.access: Check plan, credits and terms for the selected model

tools.name: Benjamin Moore Color Portfolio
tools.fit: Preview paint colors on photos and explore manufacturer color options.
tools.access: Companion visualizer; not presented as generative AI

tools.name: Microsoft Copilot
tools.fit: Explore general-purpose drafting for public or synthetic, non-sensitive material. This is not a clinical or estimating system.
tools.access: Use an organization-approved account and check current data terms and limits

useCases.title: Present three room-color directions
useCases.summary: Help a client compare wall-color ideas before buying samples.
useCases.inputs: A room photo with client permission; fixed furniture colors; preferred mood.
steps: Remove personal details from the photo and list surfaces that must stay unchanged.
Prepare three color directions; use a manufacturer visualizer to explore actual color options.
Label previews as simulations and test physical samples in daylight and evening light.
useCases.prompt: Suggest three wall-color directions for a room with warm oak cabinets and a navy sofa. Explain undertones and mood. Do not claim an exact manufacturer match from a photo.
useCases.output: A three-option concept board and physical-sample shortlist.
useCases.review: Verify real paint codes, lighting and substrate. Generated previews can change geometry or finishes.

useCases.title: Develop a client-approved mural concept
useCases.summary: Explore composition before creating original production artwork.
useCases.inputs: Client brief; wall dimensions; permitted references; required text.
steps: Create a brief with scale, palette and subjects plus any forbidden elements.
Generate varied concept directions and select one with the client.
Redraw and refine the design; prepare a scaled layout and obtain written approval.
useCases.prompt: Create a concept for a community garden mural with local plants, a calm palette and space for a title. Avoid logos and imitation of named living artists. Keep it readable at a distance.
useCases.output: A concept board, refined sketch and client approval record.
useCases.review: Check rights, lettering and feasibility. Review the selected model’s commercial terms.

useCases.title: Draft a painting scope from measured quantities
useCases.summary: Organize a clear estimate without trusting AI to measure the building.
useCases.inputs: Measured surface areas; openings; product coverage; coat count; verified rates.
steps: Measure surfaces and calculate quantities in a spreadsheet.
Use a writing assistant to organize your verified numbers into a scope with exclusions.
Recheck totals, preparation, access requirements and product specifications.
useCases.prompt: Turn the supplied verified quantities and rates into an itemized painting scope. Do not invent dimensions or prices. Separate preparation, materials, labor and exclusions; flag missing inputs.
useCases.output: A checked estimate draft and customer-facing scope.
useCases.review: A contractor verifies measurements, arithmetic, prices and exclusions. The assistant only drafts text from your verified figures.

name: Content creators
intro: Turn your expertise into original scripts, edited videos and useful follow-up posts.
caution: Use material you own or have permission to use. Check claims and media licenses, obtain consent for likenesses and voices, and follow platform disclosure requirements.

tools.name: Descript
tools.fit: Edit recorded video through its transcript and prepare captions.
tools.access: Check current recording, export and AI feature limits

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.fit: Explore image and video concepts and supporting creative assets.
tools.access: Plan and model terms vary; verify rights before publishing

useCases.title: Produce an original two-minute explainer
useCases.summary: Build a useful video around your own demonstration and verified sources.
useCases.inputs: A clear audience question; primary sources; your own demo footage.
steps: Choose one concrete problem and outline a hook, example and takeaway.
Record your demonstration, then use transcript editing to remove repetition.
Check every claim, correct captions and publish with source links.
useCases.prompt: Draft a 250-word explainer outline about [topic] using only the verified notes below. Open with the problem, demonstrate one example, explain a limitation and end with a useful takeaway. Mark unsupported claims.
useCases.output: An original script outline, edited video and reviewed captions.
useCases.review: This prompt is for a writing assistant; Descript is the editing stage. Do not copy another creator’s script.

useCases.title: Turn an interview into useful short clips
useCases.summary: Find self-contained moments without misrepresenting the speaker.
useCases.inputs: Your authorized recording; speaker consent; intended audience.
steps: Import and transcribe the recording; correct names and specialist terms.
Select excerpts with enough context and edit by transcript.
Add reviewed captions and check that each clip preserves the speaker’s meaning.
useCases.prompt: From this authorized transcript, suggest three self-contained clip candidates with an accurate title and why each is useful. Do not invent quotes or timestamps. [transcript]
useCases.output: A reviewed shortlist and captioned clips.
useCases.review: Watch the complete final clip; avoid deceptive cuts and verify permissions.

useCases.title: Create honest thumbnail concepts
useCases.summary: Communicate the real value of a video with clear visual options.
useCases.inputs: Video takeaway; original screenshots; brand palette; licensed imagery.
steps: Write a short promise that the actual video delivers.
Generate three visual directions and combine them with your own screenshots.
Check mobile readability and make sure visuals do not imply a result you did not achieve.
useCases.prompt: Create a thumbnail concept for a tutorial about [actual result]. Use a clear focal point and space for four words. Do not add fake earnings, endorsements or product features.
useCases.output: Three thumbnail concepts and one manually reviewed final design.
useCases.review: Check likeness permissions, readable text and truthful representation.

name: Developers
intro: Use coding assistants to investigate, implement and review changes with evidence.
caution: Keep secrets and customer data out of prompts. Use repository-approved tools, review generated changes and run meaningful checks before merging.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.fit: Explore coding assistance with repository and editor context.
tools.access: Free and paid offerings; check organization policy and current quotas

tools.name: GitHub Copilot documentation
tools.fit: Learn supported workflows, configuration and responsible use.

useCases.title: Investigate a Spring Boot failure
useCases.summary: Turn a sanitized error and minimal example into a testable fix.
useCases.inputs: Sanitized stack trace; Java and Spring versions; relevant source; reproduction steps.
steps: Reproduce the failure and remove credentials and customer data from logs.
Ask for ranked hypotheses and the smallest change supported by evidence.
Write a regression check, run it and review the diff before merging.
useCases.prompt: Investigate this Spring Boot failure using the provided code and versions. Separate facts from hypotheses, propose a minimal fix and explain how to verify it. Do not invent APIs. [sanitized example]
useCases.output: A reviewed patch, reproduction notes and regression evidence.
useCases.review: Verify version compatibility, security behavior and failure paths.

useCases.title: Design meaningful API tests
useCases.summary: Cover real behavior and failure cases instead of mirroring implementation.
useCases.inputs: API contract; authentication rules; boundary conditions; test framework.
steps: List observable outcomes and prioritize risky scenarios.
Draft tests for success, invalid input, authorization and downstream failures.
Run against the implementation; confirm at least one test catches the original bug.
useCases.prompt: Using this API contract, propose JUnit tests for authorization, validation and failure handling. Explain what each proves. Avoid mocking the method under test or asserting internal implementation details. [contract]
useCases.output: A risk-based test matrix and executable tests.
useCases.review: Check assertions and test isolation. Passing generated tests does not establish full correctness.

useCases.title: Review a pull request before merge
useCases.summary: Use AI to surface questions, then verify findings in code.
useCases.inputs: A focused diff; acceptance criteria; architecture constraints; test results.
steps: Provide the diff and constraints without secrets.
Request findings tied to changed lines and concrete failure scenarios.
Reproduce important findings, fix confirmed issues and have a maintainer approve.
useCases.prompt: Review this diff for correctness and security. For each finding give the trigger, impact and evidence. Mark uncertainty. Do not invent benchmarks or claim tests ran. [diff and criteria]
useCases.output: A verified review checklist with resolved findings.
useCases.review: Treat suggestions as leads. Inspect dependencies, licenses and generated code before merging.
